key_insight: Crosswind kite wakes modestly reduce lift, but rotor-slipstream treatment near the wing can reverse the predicted rotor effect.
engineering_relevance: Accurate wake and rotor modeling supports airborne wind energy performance estimates and downstream-unit placement.
method: Vortex step aerodynamics with a time-marching free vortex wake in OpenFAWE.
Lumped-mass tether and actuator-disc rotors releasing vortex rings.
Multi-kite simulations to quantify downstream wake interactions.
evidence_signal: Validation matched independent-code lift and drag within 0.3% and 0.9% for the V3 kite; a second unit one loop diameter downstream lost 2.2% of aerodynamic power.
watch_item: Free rotor rings did not converge with time-step refinement, and alternative near-wing slipstream treatments shifted the lift effect from +1.9% to −3.5%.
paper_title: Free-vortex-wake dynamics of airborne wind energy kites in crosswind flight
